# Read-only STEGO / CHAOS / BiomedCLIP audit

Audit date: 2026-09-29. All six phases completed within the read-only scope. Proposed changes below were **not applied**. No training or package installation was run. Runtime conclusions are bounded by the recorded CPU tests.

## Final report

**Method:** **Not faithful, complete or correct under the two-change constraint — high confidence.** External negatives, added losses, changed embedding/probes and missing five-crop processing alter STEGO; numerical tests also reproduce correspondence and evaluation errors (`src/train_segmentation.py:223–266,616–624`; `src/data.py:517–525,588–615`; `src/utils.py:257–305`).

**BiomedCLIP:** **Correct public weights and basic tensor dimensions; incorrect/incomplete end-to-end integration — high confidence for inspected CPU paths.** The selected tokens are unnormalized block11, the full model is not frozen/evaluated consistently, and preprocessing/cache contracts are not preserved (`src/modules.py:157–177,193–217`; `src/precompute_knns.py:51–107`; Phase3 runtime evidence).

**Reported results:** **Exact reproducibility UNVERIFIED.** Saved config differs from current config; no trained local checkpoint was found, and no NIfTI pipeline/input exists in the inspected snapshot (`logs/wandb/run-20260909_044210-y3l0vxcn/files/config.yaml:75`; `src/configs/train_config.yaml:31`; `src/data.py:141–208,400–445`; `audit/scratch/provenance.py:7–21`).

### Critical findings

**C1 — Hungarian scores and displayed labels disagree; liver can become background.** `src/utils.py:257–269` inserts missing cluster slots at `missing_entry + 1`, shifting assignments. A perfect synthetic confusion matrix scoring100% maps cluster2→background instead of liver: actual lookup `[1,0,0,0]`, required `[0,0,1,0]` (`audit/scratch/numeric_checks.py:36–39`). Main validation/evaluation use this function (`src/train_segmentation.py:428`; `src/eval_segmentation.py:174–176`). The demo has a separate indexed mapping; do not assume all output paths share this bug.

Minimal proposed replacement for `map_clusters` (preserves existing unmatched→background display policy; M1 addresses the metric inconsistency):

```diff
@@ src/utils.py:257–269 — replace function body
+        rows, cols = self.assignments
+        lookup = torch.zeros(self.n_classes + self.extra_clusters,
+                             dtype=torch.long, device=clusters.device)
+        lookup[torch.as_tensor(rows, device=clusters.device).reshape(-1)] = \
+            torch.as_tensor(cols, device=clusters.device).reshape(-1)
+        return lookup[clusters]
```

**C2 — Active augmentation loss rewards incorrect spatial matches.** Dataset coordinates are `(y,x)` (`src/data.py:588–615`); `sample` transposes their spatial axes (`src/modules.py:441–443`). Identity happens to work, but a horizontal flip samples a vertical flip. Reproduced max error15 on a4×4 ramp (`audit/scratch/numeric_checks.py:42–47`). With weight.5 this sends wrong gradients into the segmentation head (`src/configs/train_config.yaml:63`; `src/train_segmentation.py:233–244`). Minimal faithful fix is to disable this additional loss; if retaining it as a separately declared experiment, replace only its sampler as below and mask rotation padding separately:

```diff
@@ src/configs/train_config.yaml:63
-aug_alignment_weight: 0.5
+aug_alignment_weight: 0.0
@@ src/train_segmentation.py:240 — alternative only if keeping the extra loss
-                norm(sample(code, downsampled_coord_aug)),
+                norm(F.grid_sample(code, downsampled_coord_aug.flip(-1),
+                     mode="bilinear", padding_mode="reflection", align_corners=True)),
```

**C3 — The negative term separates CHAOS from an external dataset, instead of random CHAOS images.** Hard-coded external CT/MRI negatives enter every training step (`src/train_segmentation.py:157–175,616–624`), and `src/modules.py:538–561` rolls them rather than drawing random other training images. Their CT-window preprocessing also applies to MRI (`src/data.py:631–657`). This is outside both intended changes and supplies an easy dataset/modality shortcut. Saved code similarities are intra.9963/kNN.9959 versus external negative−.8451: consistent with near-constant within-domain codes, **not proof of the cause or of any particular checkpoint's predictions** (`logs/wandb/run-20260909_044210-y3l0vxcn/files/wandb-summary.json:1`).

Minimal coordinated proposal: delete the external-negative loader construction at `:616–624`, retain only the main loader, reuse its features, and exclude identity in the loss. A random nonzero cyclic shift gives uniform other-image negatives without self-pairs:

```diff
@@ src/train_segmentation.py:159
-        neg_batch = batch["neg"]
+        neg_batch = main_batch
@@ src/train_segmentation.py:175
-            neg_feats, neg_code = self.net(neg_img)
+            neg_feats, neg_code = feats, code
@@ src/train_segmentation.py:616–624 — replace external loader block
+    combined_train_loader = {"main": train_loader}
@@ src/modules.py:551–554
+        assert min_batch > 1, "Random-image negatives require batch > 1"
         for i in range(num_neg):
-            rolled_neg_feats = torch.roll(neg_feats_matched, shifts=i, dims=0)
-            rolled_neg_code = torch.roll(neg_code_matched, shifts=i, dims=0)
+            shift = torch.randint(1, min_batch, ()).item()
+            rolled_neg_feats = torch.roll(neg_feats_matched, shifts=shift, dims=0)
+            rolled_neg_code = torch.roll(neg_code_matched, shifts=shift, dims=0)
```

### Major findings

**M1 — mIoU averages a fictitious extra class.** With excess clusters, `src/utils.py:277–301` adds an unmatched bin and includes its zero IoU in the mean. Verified example:80 correct background,10 correct liver,10 unmatched-background pixels gives62.963%, versus94.444% over the two actual classes with unmatched predictions counted as errors (`audit/scratch/numeric_checks.py:40–41`). Separately, plots map unmatched clusters to background while metrics treat them as errors. Minimal numerical correction:

```diff
@@ src/utils.py:294
         iou = tp / (tp + fp + fn)
+        iou = iou[:self.n_classes]
@@ src/configs/train_config.yaml:31 — faithful baseline avoids unmatched-policy ambiguity
-extra_clusters: 20
+extra_clusters: 0
```

**M2 — Backbone extraction and freezing differ from the reference contract.** `n=2` returns the last two blocks, but `[0]` chooses block11; installed timm defaults `norm=False`. Runtime equality to raw block11 was exact; mean absolute difference from final block was.9327 (`src/modules.py:177,212–217`; installed `timm/models/vision_transformer.py:1067–1089,1156–1162`; `audit/scratch/backbone_checks.py:1–52`). Visual trunk weights are frozen, but text tower/visual projection are not, and text embeddings are made with text dropout active. Constructor moves only the trunk to CUDA before text encoding: CPU/GPU text mismatch is a source-level risk, **UNVERIFIED on CUDA** (`src/modules.py:157–172,193–198`; `src/train_segmentation.py:65–74`). Minimal extraction/freeze proposal:

```diff
@@ src/modules.py:168–172 — replace trunk-only freeze/move
+        self.full_model.requires_grad_(False)
+        self.full_model.eval().to(device)
@@ src/modules.py:197
+        self.full_model.eval()
         with torch.no_grad():
@@ src/modules.py:213
-                img, n=n, reshape=True
+                img, n=1, reshape=True, norm=True
```

Keep `device` defined before the replacement. This selects the closest reference analogue, not a proven optimal BiomedCLIP layer. Comparing normalized final versus intermediate tokens is a subsequent ablation, not grounds to silently change the baseline.

**M3 — Several extra objectives and a512-dimensional head invalidate the claimed two-change experiment.** Text mode overrides configured70 to512 (`src/train_segmentation.py:40–45`); reconstruction, augmentation, CRF-training and text entropy are active (`:227–266`). Text entropy updates the visual projection, **not the segmentation head**; tiny backward test verified that routing (`audit/scratch/backbone_checks.py:1–52`). Cluster entropy acts on hard assignments and has no gradient; centroid diversity does have gradients but is another changed objective (`src/modules.py:291–310`; `audit/scratch/numeric_checks.py:32–35`). Restore a plain baseline before evaluating additions:

```diff
@@ src/configs/train_config.yaml

+use_text_prompts: False
-text_align_weight: 0.05
+text_align_weight: 0.0
-rec_weight: 0.2
+rec_weight: 0.0
-crf_weight: 0.05
+crf_weight: 0.0
-correspondence_weight: 0.5
+correspondence_weight: 1.0
@@ src/modules.py:271,301–310
-        torch.nn.init.orthogonal_(self.clusters)
-        cluster_loss -= 0.5 * entropy
-        cluster_loss += 1.0 * diversity_loss
```

Also disable augmentation per C2 and remove text centroid initialization through `use_text_prompts=False`. Restoring70 changes head/probe shapes: old512-dimensional trained heads cannot be loaded as the same baseline. No checkpoint was edited or retrained.

Filename says `vit_base`, not BiomedCLIP/checkpoint/layer/preprocessing or ordered samples; existing files are skipped (`precompute_knns.py:75–78,106–107`). **M8 — Stopping/scheduling counts optimizer updates inconsistently.** Three manual Lightning optimizer steps increment global_step three times per batch (`src/train_segmentation.py:285–297`; installed `pytorch_lightning/loops/optimization/manual.py:99–103,135–137` and `loops/training_epoch_loop.py:113–121`). Therefore max_steps5000 permits roughly1667 head updates, while head cosine T_max5000 is stepped once per batch (`src/train_segmentation.py:525–539,661`). Historical exact update count is **UNVERIFIED**. Minimal current-three-optimizer proposal if `cfg.max_steps` is intended as head updates:

```diff
@@ src/train_segmentation.py:661

+        max_steps=3 * cfg.max_steps,
```

Checkpoint/log/reset intervals also use global_step and need the same explicitly documented units; changing only max_steps does not repair those. Paper baseline additionally requires head/probe LR.0005/.005 and the reference stopping/scheduler convention, not current warmup/cosine by assumption (`src/train_segmentation.py:525–539`; Phase1 ledger).

### Minor findings and reference-level differences

**m1 — Centering matches upstream, not literal Eq(3).** `src/modules.py:484–487` restores global feature-correlation mean. Tiny tests exactly match upstream but differ from the paper's centered expression (`audit/scratch/numeric_checks.py:18–33`). To implement literal Eq(3), delete `old_mean = fd.mean()` and `fd = fd - fd.mean() + old_mean`; keep row-mean subtraction. This decision changes shift semantics, so first choose literal-paper versus pinned-reference contract. It is not a newly introduced backbone bug.

**m2 — Diagnostic figures can misrepresent model inputs/features.** `src/vis_corr.py:110–115` uses ImageNet statistics; its “self”/“KNN” examples are other/random patient slices rather than the actual cache (`:153–159`). `src/test_timm.py:58–69` measures RGB similarity. Proposed minimal input correction: replace those means/stds with the Phase1 CLIP values; rename labels to describe the actual sampling or select IDs from the cache. Use the audit's explicit patch-feature script for quality checks.

**m3 — Plot unnormalization operates on the wrong dimension.** `src/utils.py:23–31,154–158` passes a batched tensor to an unbatched channel loop; constant images also divide by zero. Proposed minimal change at :29: `plot_img = unnorm(img.squeeze(0)).cpu().permute(1,2,0)`, preserving the optional resize above. Clamp the denominator at :31 to at least1e-8; use `rescale=False` when validating absolute preprocessing. CRF's unbatched input is unaffected.

**m4 — Dead controls and duplicate scripts obscure provenance.** `use_nns`, `use_fit_model`, `backbone_lr`, `hungarian_weight`, `reset_probe_steps`, `checkpoint_freq`, `repulsion_weight` and `stop_at_zero` do not implement their apparent controls (Phase2 citations). Root/src DINO and PiCIE copies are identical, not separate tested implementations (`audit/scratch/provenance.py:18–19`). Minimal proposal: remove unsupported config entries or fail explicitly on unsupported settings; no deletion/refactor performed. `src/test_biomedclip.py:3` imports a nonexistent Python config module before its try block; replace it with `OmegaConf.load` of the actual YAML if retaining that smoke script.

**m5 — Reference defaults themselves are not the paper's full configuration.** Current upstream uses ViT-S8, batch16, nearest image resize and different weights; it also restores correlation mean and drops extra-cluster predictions in its metric filter (Phase1 table citations). Local metric update correctly retains extra clusters. Do not “fix” it back to the upstream filtering bug. Minimal proposed paper-resize correction is `InterpolationMode.BILINEAR` for images and `NEAREST` for labels; model-card bicubic versus paper bilinear must be a declared backbone-preprocessing choice, not silently mixed.

**m6 — Saved results cannot identify today's exact implementation.** Saved extra_clusters10 differs from current20; metadata records a Git commit but not the dirty source; evaluation/demo point to absent Colab checkpoints (`logs/wandb/run-20260909_044210-y3l0vxcn/files/config.yaml:75`; `src/configs/train_config.yaml:31`; `src/configs/eval_config.yaml:14`; `src/configs/demo_config.yaml:7`). No small source diff can recover missing provenance. Minimal future addition is to save the resolved config, source diff/hash, ordered data/cache manifest and checkpoint digest with each run; request the actual checkpoint/command to verify existing results. Existing unrelated/pretrained/partial weight files must not be treated as the missing trained STEGO head.

### Missing Paper A components / backbone and CHAOS assessment

- **Missing or replaced method components:** active five-crop training/cache workflow, within-training-image random negatives, original70-dimensional head configuration, plain detached cosine clustering objective and paper/reference optimizer/update convention. Correspondence Eq(4) exists and numerically matches upstream, but the complete training objective is not Eq(5). Evidence: C3, M3, M6, M8 and Phase4 table.
- **Integration bugs:** token layer/norm mismatch; inconsistent full-model freeze/eval/device; text-loss gradient goes to a projection rather than the head; cache dropout/identity omissions; different train/demo intensity transforms; diagnostic ImageNet normalization. Public weight digest, strict key load,768 feature width,16-pixel patches, CLS removal and224/320 grid shapes passed the bounded checks (Phase3 evidence; `src/modules.py:136–175,205–217`).
- **Methodological risks:** global image-caption training does not establish organ-coherent patches; patch16 produces14×14 at224 versus upstream DINO-S8's28×28. Bilinear upsampling cannot recreate absent boundary information. Three-slice PCA/cosine panels show spatial structure but are not a segmentation-quality result (Paper B ledger; `audit/scratch/visual_checks.py:28–52`). Keep this risk separate from confirmed integration defects.
- **⚠️ Hyperparameters needing validation after correcting the baseline:** inherited affinity shifts/weights (.18/.12/.46 and.67/.25/.63), kNN7, dropout.1 and CRF sigmas; altered625 samples,20 negative repeats, LR/warmup/cosine, and K22 are not justified by any recovered BiomedCLIP/CHAOS ablation (`src/configs/train_config.yaml:15,31,47,52–87`; `src/train_segmentation.py:525–539`). There is no STEGO correspondence temperature to retune; the added text temperature.07 is a separate changed objective. No eigendecomposition/eigenbasis is required by the implemented paper contract.
- **CHAOS baseline recommendation:** CT has background+liver (K2); MRI mapping expects background+four organs (K5), but exact anatomical label identity still needs source verification (`src/data.py:57–58,348–354`; `src/configs/train_config.yaml:12–13`). Begin with those K values and disclose extra-cluster matching separately. Report foreground IoU/Dice and per-volume scores alongside pooled/background-inclusive paper metrics; pixel accuracy alone is dominated by background (Phase6 sampled foreground fractions.077–.117).
- **Intensity/geometry recommendation:** keep deterministic modality-specific normalization consistent across train/cache/eval, physically paired image/mask orientation, nearest masks and native-volume inverse geometry. Photometric jitter/blur currently feeds an unused view (`src/data.py:627–628`; `src/train_segmentation.py:161–168`); do not claim those augmentations were evaluated. Any MRI bias-field/intensity augmentation or further CT window change should be a declared domain experiment, not another silent modification. Resolution320 has working positional interpolation but remains a distribution/resolution change requiring separate validation.

### Prioritized fix order (future work only)

1. Resolve the actual run/checkpoint and preprocessing manifest; preserve the current data and results. Establish a patient-level canonical-ID split and fixed evaluation protocol before comparing scores (M5, m6).
2. Correct LUT/mIoU and augmentation alignment, then restore within-CHAOS negatives and the plain Eq(5) baseline (C1–C3, M1, M3). Old metrics/pictures should be re-evaluated from the actual checkpoint after metric fixes, not retrospectively guessed.
3. Make frozen feature extraction/preprocessing deterministic, choose and document the normalized final-token baseline, then regenerate identity-checked kNN caches after separate authorization (M2, M4, M5).
4. Restore five-crop routing and explicit update-count/LR conventions; implement the requested NIfTI/volume path if NIfTI is the intended source (M6, M8). Correct CRF confidence/device handling and fail explicitly when semantic mapping is missing (M7, M10).
5. Run the future controls in Phase6 and then ablate dense-feature layer, K, shifts, sampling, resolution and domain augmentations one at a time. New trained baselines are required after head/objective changes; no such training was run here.

## Scope and evidence conventions

Only this report and small scripts in `audit/scratch/` may be created or changed. No training, package installation, dataset/checkpoint changes, or project fixes are authorized. Binary observations cite the audit script and recorded output because binary files have no source line numbers. PDFs are cited by filename, page, section/equation; PDF files do not have source lines. Source citations use repository-relative `file:line`. `ref/` means upstream STEGO at commit `eb4d6b521740bd4265681b353547f2ffca65d673`, at https://github.com/mhamilton723/STEGO/tree/eb4d6b521740bd4265681b353547f2ffca65d673 .

Working tree initially had existing changes in `.DS_Store`, `src/configs/train_config.yaml`, `src/modules.py`, `src/preprocess.py`, `src/train_segmentation.py`, `src/vis_corr.py`; untracked Dataset, correspondence images, README and `src/stego.pdf`. HEAD was `c859758`. Existing changes are part of the audited snapshot, not produced by this audit. Which revision/config produced reported results is UNVERIFIED.

## 1. Ground truth (Phase 1)

### Paper A ledger — `2203.08414v1.pdf`

- §3.1, p3, Eq(1): channel-normalized spatial cosine correlations `F[n,h,w,i,j] = sum_c normalize(f)[n,c,h,w] normalize(g)[n,c,i,j]`.
- §3.2, p5, Eq(2): preliminary loss `-sum((F-b)*S)`; not the final training loss.
- Eq(3): spatial centering over target positions only, `Fsc = F - mean_ij(F)`.
- Eq(4): final correlation loss `-sum((Fsc-b)*max(S,0))`. No temperature. Zero-clamp applies to segmentation similarity, not backbone similarity.
- §3.3, p6, Eq(5): weighted self + kNN + random-image versions of Eq(4). Frozen backbone; global average pooling of dense features; cosine kNN; uniformly sample one of top seven excluding self. Random minibatch pairing excludes self. Five half-size crops are separate neighbors (A.12 p26).
- A.10 p24: DINO ViT-Base teacher weights; final spatial activations; channel dropout p=.1; linear head plus two-layer ReLU MLP, output 70; Adam head LR .0005, batch 32; sample 121 spatial positions using grid sampling; independent online cosine minibatch k-means and supervised linear probes, separate Adam optimizers LR .005. Probe labels do not train segmentation features (§4.1 p8).
- A.10/Table 6: Cityscapes `(lambda_rand,lambda_knn,lambda_self)=(.91,.58,1)`, `(b_rand,b_knn,b_self)=(.31,.18,.46)`; CocoStuff `(.15,1,.10)` and `(1,.20,.12)`. §3.3's rough ratio self≈rand≈2knn differs from these dataset-specific table values. A.11 p25 says balance of attraction/repulsion must be checked via cosine distributions; too much attraction produces too few clusters.
- A.10: five crops at half original height/width; train minor-axis resize 224 then center crop 224; eval 320 then center crop 320; bilinear images, nearest labels. CRF 10 iterations, bilateral weight 4/spatial sigma 67/color sigma 3; smoothness weight 3/spatial sigma 1. Core algorithm does not require reconstruction, augmentation-alignment, CRF-training loss, eigendecomposition or an explicit spectral basis. Eq(6–7) give the graph-energy interpretation, not additional optimized losses.
- §4.1 pp7–8: 27 classes for CocoStuff/Cityscapes, Potsdam-3 A.2; corpus-level Hungarian cluster alignment; pixel accuracy and mIoU; separate linear probe. Dice and per-volume metrics are not paper protocol. Epoch count, stopping criterion, random-negative repeat count, precise image normalization and patch size are not specified in the recorded implementation-details text: use explicit reference configuration below, not assumptions.

### Paper B ledger — `2303.00915v3.pdf`

- Supplementary Note pp20–22/Table 2: ViT-B/16, hidden dimension 768, 16×16 patches; selected input resolution 224 (14×14 patches); Table 4/5 studies 384, but final selected model uses 224. ImageNet-pretrained initialization, subsequently biomedical image-text training. Text encoder PubMedBERT context 256.
- Supplement Eq(1), p20: symmetric image-to-text and text-to-image InfoNCE, matched image-caption positives, all other in-batch pairs negative; cosine scores divided by learnable temperature. This trains global alignment, not STEGO spatial correspondence or DINO self-distillation.
- Table 9 p22: image mean `(0.48145466,0.4578275,0.40821073)`, std `(0.26862954,0.26130258,0.27577711)`; RandomResizedCrop; AdamW peak LR 5e-4, decay .2, betas .9/.98, eps 1e-6, cosine LR, 32 epochs, 2000 warmup, seed 0; chosen batch 4k (p22). This is backbone pretraining, not downstream STEGO training.
- Official `open_clip_config.json:3–9,19–29` confirms 512-dimensional projected embedding, timm `vit_base_patch16_224`, linear visual projection and 224 input; matching mean/std. Source: https://huggingface.co/microsoft/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224/blob/main/open_clip_config.json . CLS/pooling/projection implementation must be checked against installed loader; the paper does not define its Python output API. Patch features for STEGO must be pre-pooling 768-dimensional tokens, not the 512-dimensional global image embedding.

### Table (a): component contract (Phase 1 checkpoint)

| Component | Paper A eq/section | Reference file:line | Expected behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frozen teacher/dense activations | §3.1–3.3, A.10 | ref/src/modules.py:17–118 | Frozen DINO, last normalized spatial tokens, remove CLS; 384 small / 768 base; optional keys path is not default |
| Segmentation head | A.10 | ref/src/modules.py:73–81,108–118 | Linear 1×1 plus C→C→70 ReLU MLP; dropout .1 |
| Cosine correspondence | Eq(1) | ref/src/modules.py:275–288,325–345 | Normalize channels, all spatial pairs; grid_sample align_corners=True |
| Spatial centering | Eq(3) | ref/src/modules.py:330–333 | **Reference deviates:** subtract row mean then restore batch global mean; paper does not restore it |
| Final pair loss | Eq(4) | ref/src/modules.py:335–347,393–398 | Negative shifted affinity × nonnegative code cosine; reference averages, paper writes sums |
| Self/kNN/random weighted total | Eq(5) | ref/src/modules.py:355–398; ref/src/train_segmentation.py:154–181 | Same-image self loss, sampled neighbor, shuffled negative, weighted sum; no contrastive temperature |
| Random pairing | §3.3 | ref/src/modules.py:291–295 | No self-pair for batch >1; implementation's repaired permutation can repeat targets (not strict shuffle); batch 1 cannot provide negative |
| Image kNN | §3.3 | ref/src/precompute_knns.py:15–21,66–96; ref/src/data.py:503–524 | Normalized GAP dense features, cosine top-30 cache; choose ranks 1–7 assuming rank0=self; dataset ordering fixed |
| Five crops | §3.3/A.10/A.12 | ref/src/crop_datasets.py:62–74,90–123,140–143 | Half-sized five crops before kNN; matching image/label geometry |
| Preprocessing/augmentation | A.10 | ref/src/utils.py:140–183; ref/src/train_segmentation.py:408–450 | ImageNet normalization for DINO; train224/eval320 center crop. **Reference deviates:** nearest image resize at utils:180 versus paper bilinear; extra photometric/geometry branch exists but default alignment weight0 |
| Online cosine clustering | §3.3/A.10 | ref/src/modules.py:134–161; ref/src/train_segmentation.py:213–237 | Gaussian initial centroids, hard assignments for training, negative assigned cosine, detached codes; independent Adam .005 |
| Linear probe | §4.1/A.10 | ref/src/train_segmentation.py:75–90,210–230 | Train 1×1 classifier with CE on detached codes; no supervised gradient into head |
| Inference | §3.3/§4.1 | ref/src/eval_segmentation.py:120–141 | Average original/horizontal-flip codes; bilinear code resize; class-axis argmax; alpha2 for cluster CRF logits |
| CRF refinement | A.10 | ref/src/crf.py:13–44 | 10 mean-field iterations; specified bilateral and spatial terms |
| Hungarian + mIoU/accuracy | §4.1 | ref/src/utils.py:219–274 | Accumulate full validation confusion; Hungarian maximizes pixel count; absent-class IoU omitted. **Reference bug:** update filters predictions <n_classes, dropping extra clusters |
| Optimization/stopping | A.10 | ref/src/train_segmentation.py:373–383,403,482–491; ref/src/configs/train_config.yml:9–64 | Adam .0005/.005, no scheduler, seed0, default max_steps5000. Reference default batch16/ViT-S8 differs from paper batch32/ViT-Base; steps not epochs |

### Phase 2 conclusions and executable roles

- The exhaustive inventory above covers 61,327 pre-existing files including hidden/ignored files and every containing directory (`audit/scratch/inventory.py:22–43`). `.git/` is repository/editor metadata; `__pycache__/` and `src/__pycache__/` are compiled caches; `data/` is empty. No STEGO `.ckpt` is present under `checkpoints/`; the only learned local backbone is `src/BiomedCLIP-PubMedBERT_256-vit_base_patch16_224/open_clip_pytorch_model.bin`. `models/` contains older MoCo/PiCIE artifacts and an unfinished `.tmp` download, none selected by the active BiomedCLIP branch (`src/train_segmentation.py:47–55`; inventory; provenance output).
- Active entrypoints: `src/preprocess.py:222–241` creates CT PNG volumes/splits; `src/data.py:87–445,480–657` loads raw DICOM or processed PNG and constructs pairs; `src/precompute_knns.py:24–107` caches neighbors; `src/modules.py:122–248,265–315,468–572` supplies backbone/head/probe/loss; `src/train_segmentation.py:547–674` trains; `src/eval_segmentation.py:61–181` evaluates; `src/crf.py:13–44` refines; `src/utils.py:149–209,229–307` transforms and measures; `src/demo_segmentation.py:145–305` independently maps clusters and renders predictions. Four config files select train, eval, demo and plotting, not one immutable experiment.
- Competing preprocessing: `src/chaos.py:44–55,62–100` converts raw DICOM with per-slice min/max and patients 1/2 as validation into `CHAOS/...`; `src/preprocess.py:56–58,148–152,230–239` uses isotropic CT resampling, [-400,400] and last lexically sorted 20% patients; raw loading in `src/data.py:239–339` uses body crop/pad, in-plane resampling and [-150,250]. Active processed loader reads `preprocessed/`, **not** `Dataset/CHAOS/` (`src/data.py:356–391`). These artifacts are not interchangeable.
- Dataset roots contain DICOM/PNG, no `.nii` or `.nii.gz` in either dataset tree (provenance script output). No NIfTI loader was found in the executable data/preprocessing paths. Requested NIfTI-to-feature contract is missing, not assumed equivalent to DICOM.
- `src/crop_datasets.py:76–117` writes five crops, but `src/data.py:517–525` always constructs CHAOS directly and never loads those cropped outputs; `crop_type` only labels cache filenames at :549–551. `src/chaos.py` executes conversion at import (:84 onward), and installs pydicom if missing (:37–41); it was not imported/run.
- Duplicated root and `src/` copies of both `dino/` and `picie/` are byte-identical (provenance output); running `src/train_segmentation.py` resolves the `src/` copies. DINO/FPN classes remain optional branches, not proof the selected backbone is DINO (`src/train_segmentation.py:47–55`). `train_cluster_probe` and `_add_spatial_coords` are constructed/defined but unused by the active training loss (`:82,128–141,280`). `use_nns`, `use_fit_model`, `backbone_lr`, `hungarian_weight`, `reset_probe_steps`, `checkpoint_freq`, `repulsion_weight`, `stop_at_zero` do not control the active corresponding behavior; compare config values with training :148–306,519–544,658–674 and dataset :543–556.
- Diagnostic scripts: `src/plot_dino_correspondence.py:39–49,99–104` can inspect BiomedCLIP despite its name; `src/vis_corr.py:61–115` independently duplicates transforms with ImageNet statistics, so its figures do not reproduce training inputs. `src/test_timm.py:58–69` computes pixel RGB cosine, not learned token cosine. `src/test_biomedclip.py:6–35` is a shape smoke script. `src/plot_pr_curves.py:83–84,131,152,226` retains undefined `self.dino`, old Lightning hook and `.yml` config; `src/plot_potsdam.py:12` and `src/train_crf.py:35` are legacy natural-image/CRF experiments. `show_rgb.py`, `count_empty_labels.py` are dataset visual/count utilities; download scripts are provisioning, not training. `STEGO_Colab_Demo.ipynb`, `README.md`, `stego.pdf` and `results/figures/` are reference/demo material, not evidence of CHAOS accuracy. No paper reread was performed for the duplicate PDF.
- Tests cover selected formulas/fixtures, not real BiomedCLIP loading. `src/tests/test_train_segmentation.py:17–33` only checks coordinate concatenation; `.github/workflows/tests.yml:19–22` omits OpenCLIP/timm; `src/tests/test_modules.py:118` expects entropy coefficient 1.5 while current `src/modules.py:304` uses .5. Full pytest was not run because fixtures write datasets and temporary files outside the permitted script-only output contract.
- Historical results are attributable only to saved logs, not a validated checkpoint. Latest completed summary found: `logs/wandb/run-20260909_044210-y3l0vxcn/files/wandb-summary.json:1`: cluster mIoU30.7159%, accuracy92.1427%, linear mIoU87.46875%; saved config `.../config.yaml:75` has CT, text prompts, 10 extra clusters, layer_n2. Its `wandb-metadata.json:5–15` identifies `src/train_segmentation.py`, commit c859758 and Python3.14. Current config has **20** extra clusters (`src/configs/train_config.yaml:31`). Metadata does not snapshot uncommitted source. Actual exact code/checkpoint that generated those results remains **UNVERIFIED**. Default eval/demo point to missing Colab paths and a 46.8485 checkpoint (`src/configs/eval_config.yaml:2,14`; `src/configs/demo_config.yaml:4,7`); that number is a filename, not verified evaluation evidence.

## 5. Silent-failure hunt (Phase 5)

- **Mixed processed datasets are currently loaded together:** active CT train4475=2606 new `CT_<pid>_<slice>` +1869 legacy `CT_p<pid>_s<index>`; validation1101=629+472. Same patient appears under two identifiers within each split. Preprocessor creates directories but never establishes a manifest/cleans prior variants (`preprocess.py:180–183,211–217`), loader accepts all filenames (`data.py:377–391`). Actual three-slice panel shows contrast/noise differences; producing transform of old PNGs UNVERIFIED. These are not train/val leakage in the inspected snapshot, but duplicate/mixed views bias sampling, kNN and reported volume weighting.
- **Salience coordinates off by one/non-square:** `modules.py:463` divides both axes by height rather than [W−1,H−1]. For an actual bottom-right (3,5) pixel of4×6, output(1.5,.5), expected(1,1), and reflection sampling folds the invalid x coordinate. Even square inputs miss exact end points. Salience thresholds are computed after CLIP normalization (`data.py:441–444`); comments assuming sums in[0,3] do not match actual normalized range.
- **Potential label/order loss:** raw pairing uses independently sorted DICOM and PNG lists (`data.py:171–180,199–208`); missing middle mask shifts subsequent pairings. `preprocess.py:100–103` maps by filename order, not verified per-slice identifier. It assigns CT geometry to a PNG stack without proving orientation (:108–111); mismatched counts bypass reorder, then errors may be swallowed per patient (:238–241). Sampled overlays do not prove all volumes are correct. Require source slice IDs/physical positions/count checks to verify remainder.
- **MRI silently clipped:** same CT-window function is used for MRI (`data.py:215–236,425–426`); T1/T2 have no HU contract. Preprocessed raw-label lookup accepts only exact0/63/126/189/252 (`data.py:58,348–354`); any different encoded values become ignore, not a detected data error. CT mask0/255→0/1 is verified on sampled labels; all-source MRI anatomical identity/encoding remains UNVERIFIED until metadata/source conventions and sampled masks are checked.
- **Missing labels/blank prediction paths:** absent masks become all−1 (`data.py:414–415,438–439`); CE on no valid pixels is not guarded (`train_segmentation.py:268–277`). `demo_segmentation.py:169–171,224–225` returns an all-background map if assignment acquisition fails; morphology may delete remaining small components. Do not attribute blank outputs solely to backbone quality while these deterministic paths exist.
- **CUDA-only evaluation fault:** CRF predictions explicitly move to CPU while labels stay on model device (`eval_segmentation.py:114–115,140–147`). `utils.py:249` combines their boolean masks, causing a device mismatch on CUDA. CPU execution works; GPU failure remains UNVERIFIED by execution because no CUDA device is available.
- **Visualization unnormalization:** `prep_for_plot` unsqueezes to[1,3,H,W] (`utils.py:23–31`), but `UnNormalize` iterates first axis assuming[3,H,W] (:154–158), applying first-channel mean/std to every channel. Plot min/max then masks the error and divides by zero for a constant image (:31). CRF passes an unbatched tensor and is not affected by this batching defect.
- **Unavailable/no-op controls:** use_nns=False does not disable cache loading; use_fit_model/backbone_lr do not fine-tune visual trunk; hungarian_weight and reset_probe_steps do not affect optimization; spatial_weight/_add_spatial_coords unused. Citations in Phase2; do not interpret these config names as implemented behavior.
- **No evidence of additional hidden gradient/dtype/broadcast failures in tested branches:** synthetic corr/probe/CRF computations finite; shapes explicit; masks int64, inputs/features FP32. The salience rectangular/augmentation failures above are reproduced; checkpoint inference, CUDA, full MRI workflow, and full trainer callbacks remain UNVERIFIED. This is a bounded audit, not proof of absence of every possible failure.

**Phase 5 complete.**

### Future expensive controls — NOT RUN

Exact commands, from the project root, are below. They use the opt-in script `audit/scratch/future_baselines.py:1–74`, do not install packages or save checkpoints, and are **not executed as part of this read-only audit**. Its four training/four held-out-patient examples use only the current `CT_<pid>` family to avoid knowingly mixing legacy transforms. These are supervised decoder controls on frozen patch features, **not full STEGO training or an estimate of its unsupervised score**; they isolate representation/label plumbing before any expensive end-to-end experiment.

```sh
/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/python3 -B audit/scratch/future_baselines.py --mode overfit --steps 1000 --allow-training
/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/python3 -B audit/scratch/future_baselines.py --mode shuffled-label --steps 1000 --allow-training
/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/python3 -B audit/scratch/future_baselines.py --mode random-feature --steps 1000 --allow-training
```

- **Few-slice overfit:** expected training CE reduction and higher foreground IoU than the two controls; perfect native-boundary reconstruction is not expected from a14×14 token grid. Failure to improve is a reason to inspect labels/coordinates/features, not proof that longer training will fix it. The exact outcome/threshold is UNVERIFIED until run.
- **Shuffled-label control:** fixed within-slice pixel permutations preserve class frequencies and remove spatial anatomical correspondence. Expected weak true-liver/held-out IoU despite potentially high background accuracy. This intentionally tests only the supervised decoder. In actual STEGO, shuffling probe labels must not change the unsupervised head/cluster optimization when RNG and other inputs are held fixed, because probe inputs are detached (`src/train_segmentation.py:271–281`); the numerical detach check already passed (`audit/scratch/numeric_checks.py:55–56`).
- **Random-feature control:** fixed independent random spatial features replace the pretrained features for both splits. It may memorize the tiny training set; expected poor held-out foreground transfer. Similar held-out performance to pretrained features would undermine a claim that BiomedCLIP contributes useful dense information. This is a diagnostic hypothesis, not a measured result.

A genuine full-STEGO controlled ablation requires C1–C3/M1–M8 resolved and the requested dataset/checkpoint contract. No existing command implements that corrected baseline; claiming a current training invocation would run the paper-faithful experiment would be false. Raw-NIfTI tracing remains UNVERIFIED because the input and loader are absent. Checkpoint round-trip/inference, CUDA execution, exhaustive volume orientation and all MRI anatomical mappings remain UNVERIFIED; they require the actual checkpoint, matching hardware, and source label/geometry metadata respectively.

Final audit integrity check: all scratch scripts parse as Python; the future controls were not executed. Local source citations were checked for file existence and starting-line range. Git status retains the original modified/untracked project paths plus `audit/`; no audit tool wrote an existing project file. Runtime write/network guards are defined in `audit/scratch/guard.py:1–27`. This status comparison is not a claim that a before/after cryptographic snapshot of every project file was taken.

**Phase 6 complete.** No real-data optimizer step, long job, package install, dataset/cache regeneration or checkpoint modification was performed. Proposed fixes and future commands are review artifacts only.
